Q: UDP sendto() succeeds but outgoing UDP packet is not transmitted while receiving 500 Mbps UDP stream on Windows A:

sendto() succeeding only means Winsock (Windows Sockets) accepted the datagram into its buffer for transmission, it does not guarantee that the packet has reached the NIC driver or gone out onto the physical wire.

Since this issue persists across both Python and PowerShell, the bottleneck is almost certainly below the application layer in the NIC/NDIS driver stack. At a ~500 Mbps incoming stream rate, receive-side processing, DPC/interrupt moderation load, or NIC queue congestion can starve or drop outgoing packets after Winsock accepts them.

Furthermore, do not rely solely on Wireshark on the sending host to prove the packet wasn't transmitted. Under heavy traffic (~500 Mbps), Npcap (Wireshark's packet capture driver) can drop capture events in the kernel buffer even if the NIC actually sends the frame out.

A few things worth trying to isolate and fix the issue:

  • Capture externally: Sniff traffic on the receiving host (FPGA/network switch port) rather than relying on Wireshark on the sending machine.

  • Check NIC Driver Settings:

    • Enable RSS so incoming UDP processing is distributed across multiple CPU cores rather than pinning a single core.

    • Adjust Interrupt Moderation or temporarily disable UDP Checksum Offload / Large Send Offload (LSO) in the NIC advanced properties to see if the driver is bottlenecking.

  • Dedicated Control Socket/Port: you could also try using a dedicated, persistent UDP socket bound to a separate port exclusively for outgoing STOP commands rather than recreating threads or sharing the high-throughput receive socket.

Q: Query a list of all Cosmos DBs across many subscriptions A:

Your query has a couple of issues, and there's a simpler approach. The good news is that all Cosmos DB APIs actually share a single resource type: Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseaccounts. The API type (SQL, MongoDB, Cassandra, Gremlin, Table, PostgreSQL vCore) is stored as a property on that resource, not as a separate resource type.

The types you included are wrong:

  • Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/databaseaccounts — this is Azure Database for PostgreSQL (a separate product, not Cosmos DB)

  • Microsoft.DBforMariaDB/databaseaccounts — same issue, this is Azure Database for MariaDB

Correct Query

To list all Cosmos DB accounts regardless of API:

Resources
| where type =~ "Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseaccounts"
| project name, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, location,
          kind,
          apiType = tostring(properties.capabilities)

To See Which API Each Account Uses

The API kind is reflected in the kind property and/or properties.capabilities:

Resources
| where type =~ "Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseaccounts"
| project
    name,
    resourceGroup,
    subscriptionId,
    location,
    kind,                                           // e.g. "GlobalDocumentDB", "MongoDB", "Parse"
    capabilities = tostring(properties.capabilities) // e.g. "EnableCassandra", "EnableGremlin", "EnableTable"
| order by name asc

API-to-Kind Mapping

Cosmos DB APIkind valuecapabilities entryNoSQL (SQL)GlobalDocumentDB(none)MongoDBMongoDB(none, or MongoDBv3.4)CassandraGlobalDocumentDBEnableCassandraGremlinGlobalDocumentDBEnableGremlinTableGlobalDocumentDBEnableTablePostgreSQL (vCore)GlobalDocumentDBEnableMongo or separate cluster resource*

Note on Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL: Newer Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL (vCore-based clusters) use the resource type Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/serverGroupsv2, which is genuinely a separate resource type. If you need those too, you can union them:

Resources
| where type =~ "Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseaccounts"
    or type =~ "Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/serverGroupsv2"
| project name, type, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, location

This will give you a truly complete picture across all subscriptions.

Q: Curl file download using ftp protocol fail with RETR response 550 A:

Change the path format as such:

curl -u test:test 'ftp://10.226.45.7/%2fhome/test/README.txt' -o /home/dccom/testserver/db/log/README.txt
